courses.name: B.Sc. in Allied Health Sciences
aliases: B.Sc. Anaesthesia and Operation Theatre Technology
courses.summary: A B.Sc. in Allied Health Sciences is a bachelor's degree that trains health technologists and health-science professionals who work alongside doctors and nurses. Programmes usually specialise in one field, such as anaesthesia and operation theatre technology, medical imaging and radiography, dialysis, cardiac care, emergency and trauma care, neuro-electrophysiology or clinical research. They combine anatomy, physiology and pathology with specialist theory and supervised hospital training. Many run for three years plus an internship. Registration and recognition rules differ by profession and country.

universities.name: Rajas Institute of Allied Health Sciences
universities.summary: Rajas Institute of Allied Health Sciences (RIAHS) is a private self-financing college at Raja Nagar, Vadakkankulam, Tirunelveli District, Tamil Nadu, affiliated to The Tamil Nadu Dr. M.G.R. Medical University, which awards its degrees. It offers two four-year B.Sc. courses, Cardiac Technology and Operation Theatre and Anaesthesia Technology, with 10 seats each. Admission is domestic-only: no route for foreign nationals, NRIs or OCI holders is published.
universities.campusLifestyle: RIAHS teaches at Raja Nagar, Vadakkankulam, with seven named laboratories: anatomy, physiology, biochemistry, pathology, microbiology, a skills lab and a computer lab. The physiology lab lists treadmills, metabolic carts, cardiac monitors and drug infusion pumps. The college also lists a library, smart classrooms, lecture halls and an examination centre. It has 13 listed teaching staff, including a principal, a vice principal and two course directors.
universities.cityProfile: RIAHS is at Raja Nagar, Vadakkankulam, Tirunelveli District, Tamil Nadu 627116. Its clinical training runs mainly through hospitals in Tirunelveli and Nagercoil, with further tie-ups in Valliyur, Chennai, Puducherry and Thiruvananthapuram, so students should expect postings away from the campus. RIAHS is one of five colleges of Rajas Medical Institutions, a group founded in 1987 by Sardar Dr. S.A. Raja; its sister colleges cover dentistry, pharmacy, nursing and laboratory medicine. The academic year starts on 1 August.
universities.practicalExposure: RIAHS trains students through tie-ups with 20 hospitals and memoranda of understanding with Bethesda Hospital, Nagercoil, and The Salvation Army Catherine Booth Hospital. Partners include Angel Hospital, Kauvery Hospital and Porunai Hospital in Tirunelveli; Ponjesly Super Speciality Hospital and KIMS Hospital in Nagercoil; Rajiv Gandhi Government General Hospital and the Tamil Nadu Government Multi Super Speciality Hospital, Omandurar, in Chennai; and Indira Gandhi Government General Hospital and Post Graduate Institute, Puducherry. Each degree ends with a one-year compulsory internship. Cardiac Technology interns spend three months each in the cath lab and blood bank, echo room, intensive coronary care unit and Holter (ambulatory ECG). Operation Theatre and Anaesthesia Technology interns rotate through the sterilisation room, recovery room, surgical ICU and operation theatres. University rules require 100 per cent attendance in practical and clinical areas before the degree is awarded.
universities.hostelOverview: RIAHS lists a hostel among its facilities and has a Hostel Committee, but it publishes no room types, capacity, gender arrangements or hostel fees. Ask the college for current hostel availability and charges before planning accommodation.
universities.dietarySupport: RIAHS lists a campus cafeteria among its facilities. It publishes no menu, meal plan or prices, and no separate mess charge is listed.
universities.safetyOverview: RIAHS lists a Discipline Committee and a Hostel Committee among its 17 committees, each convened by staff named on the college website. The college does not publish its anti-ragging or campus security arrangements.
universities.studentSupport: RIAHS names committees for admission, academics, hospital training, scholarships, certificate verification and university registration, each with named staff. Transport runs between the campus and designated locations; routes and charges are not published.

faq.question: Is Rajas Institute of Allied Health Sciences a university?
faq.answer: No. RIAHS is a private self-financing college affiliated to The Tamil Nadu Dr. M.G.R. Medical University, Chennai, under institution code 898. The university sets the syllabus, conducts the annual examinations and awards the B.Sc. degree. RIAHS belongs to Rajas Medical Institutions and is run by the Selvam Educational and Charitable Trust.

faq.question: Which courses does RIAHS offer?
faq.answer: RIAHS offers two degrees: B.Sc Cardiac Technology and B.Sc Operation Theatre and Anaesthesia Technology. Each runs three academic years plus a one-year compulsory internship, and the university's 2025-26 list sanctions 10 seats for each. RIAHS offers no diploma, postgraduate, nursing, physiotherapy or pharmacy course.

faq.question: Can international students, NRIs or OCI holders apply to RIAHS?
faq.answer: RIAHS is listed as domestic-only. Neither RIAHS nor The Tamil Nadu Dr. M.G.R. Medical University publishes an admission route, quota, fee or document list for foreign nationals, NRIs or OCI cardholders. Applicants outside India should get written confirmation from the college before applying.

faq.question: What are the eligibility requirements?
faq.answer: Under the university's regulations, applicants need a pass in 10+2 with Physics, Chemistry and Biology, or Botany and Zoology, scoring at least 35 per cent in each subject including English. They must be 17 by 31 December of the admission year. Applicants from boards other than the Tamil Nadu Higher Secondary need a university eligibility certificate.

faq.question: How do I apply to RIAHS?
faq.answer: Apply directly through the RIAHS online application form, which asks for course choice, Aadhaar number, community category, nationality and parent details. These two courses are not offered through Tamil Nadu government-quota paramedical counselling at self-financing colleges, so the college fills its seats itself.

faq.question: When does the course start and when do admissions close?
faq.answer: The university's regulations set 1 August as the start of the academic year and 30 September as the last date for any admission, even if seats remain vacant. Students admitted by then sit the first-year university examination the following August.

faq.question: What are the fees at RIAHS?
faq.answer: RIAHS does not publish tuition, hostel or other fees. Because these courses are not filled through government-quota counselling, no government-fixed fee applies. Ask the college for its current fee schedule in writing before paying.

faq.question: What language are classes taught in?
faq.answer: English. The university's B.Sc. allied health regulations make English the medium of instruction and examination for all subjects.

faq.question: Where do students do clinical training?
faq.answer: RIAHS lists tie-ups with 20 hospitals, including Angel, Kauvery and Porunai hospitals in Tirunelveli, Ponjesly and KIMS hospitals in Nagercoil, and government general hospitals in Chennai and Puducherry. It has memoranda of understanding with Bethesda Hospital, Nagercoil, and The Salvation Army Catherine Booth Hospital.

faq.question: What are the attendance and progression rules?
faq.answer: Students need 75 per cent attendance in theory and 100 per cent in practical and clinical work, with no condonation. They move to the third year only after passing all first- and second-year subjects, and must complete the course within six years of joining.
